note: Every rate here is verified against the bank's own official page on the 'updated' date (headless-Chrome render, since bank pages are JS-locked). Refresh monthly. 'verified:false' = published rate we haven't browser-confirmed yet. 'watch' and 'suits' feed the drawer's help layer (not indexed — served from a script object).

fd.note: As published by RHB (rates on their PDF sheet); verifying. Min S$20,000, 3–36 month terms.
fd.watch: You'll need to lock S$20,000 in for the full term to earn the top rate.
fd.suits: Savers with a larger sum they won't touch for a year.

fd.note: Lowest entry of the higher-rate banks — just S$500. Rate as published; verifying.
fd.watch: One of the very few banks paying a top rate with a tiny minimum.
fd.suits: Anyone starting small — you only need S$500 to get going.

fd.note: The rate steps up over the 12-month term; the effective (average) rate you earn is 1.50% p.a.
fd.watch: Fresh funds only — money already with Maybank won't earn the promo, and it renews at the lower board rate after the term unless you move it.
fd.suits: Savers bringing in new money they can set aside for the full year.

fd.note: 1.50% on 4–5 month fresh funds; 1.45% for 12 months at S$20,000.
fd.watch: The 1.50% is on a short 4–5 month term with fresh funds; the 12-month rate is a touch lower at 1.45%.
fd.suits: Savers who want a strong rate but a shorter lock-in.

fd.watch: Personal Banking earns 1.45%; Preferred clients get 1.50% on the same term.
fd.suits: Savers comfortable with a 9-month term from S$10,000.

fd.note: 1.40% via e-banking (min S$500 online / S$20,000 at branch). Verifying exact tenor.
fd.watch: The best rate is via e-banking, where the minimum is just S$500 (branch placements need S$20,000).
fd.suits: Savers who bank online and want a low entry.

fd.note: 1.35% p.a. if you also hold eligible wealth products.
fd.watch: Holding eligible UOB wealth products lifts the rate to 1.35%.
fd.suits: Existing UOB customers, or anyone who wants a mainstream local bank.

fd.watch: You get 1.30% placing online versus 1.25% at a branch.
fd.suits: OCBC customers who can place S$20,000 online.

fd.note: By customer tier: 1.30% standard, 1.40% Priority, 1.60% Priority Private.
fd.watch: The rate rises with your banking tier — 1.40% for Priority, 1.60% for Priority Private.
fd.suits: Priority and Private banking clients get the most from this one.

fd.note: The easiest to start — just S$1,000, and no fresh-funds condition.
fd.watch: The lowest rate here, but there's no fresh-funds condition and it's the simplest to open.
fd.suits: Anyone who wants to start small and simple — just S$1,000.

savings.note: Top rate needs salary credit + transactions across several categories (cards, loans, insurance).
savings.watch: You reach the top rate only by stacking several categories; fewer categories means a lower rate.
savings.suits: People who already run their salary, cards and loans through DBS.
steps: Credit your salary or income to DBS (GIRO or PayLah!).
Transact in the bonus categories: card spend, home loan, insurance, investments.
The full 4.1% needs your salary + 3 categories + a high monthly total (around S$30,000).
Salary + just one category earns far less (roughly 1.8%).

savings.note: Credit salary / GIRO + spend S$500 on an eligible card.
savings.watch: You need to credit your salary or GIRO and spend at least S$500 on an eligible card each month.
savings.suits: Salaried spenders who can comfortably hit the monthly card spend.
steps: Credit your salary (about S$1,600+) via GIRO or PayNow.
Spend at least S$500 a month on an eligible UOB One card.
Do both to earn up to ~3.4% (the top rate applies in steps, up to S$150,000).

savings.note: Digital bank — no salary, spend or hoops. Simplest high rate.
savings.watch: A flat rate with almost no conditions — no salary credit or card spend needed.
savings.suits: Anyone who wants a high rate without the hoops.
steps: Nothing to do — it's a flat rate. No salary credit, no card spend, no lock-in.

savings.watch: The rate is linked to card spend, but the conditions are light.
savings.suits: NTUC / FairPrice shoppers, and anyone wanting simple high interest.
steps: Light conditions tied to card spend; no salary credit needed.

savings.note: About 1.95% on salary + save + spend; reaches 4.45% when you also insure and invest.
savings.watch: 1.95% comes from salary + save + spend; it climbs toward 4.45% only if you also insure and invest.
savings.suits: OCBC customers who can stack a few of the bonus categories.
steps: Credit your salary (S$1,800+) — the biggest single bonus.
Grow your balance by at least S$500 a month ('Save').
Spend S$500 on an OCBC card — that gets you to about 1.95%.
Add Insure and Invest to push toward 4.45%. Bonuses apply on your first S$100,000.
